notes.capacity: Planning allowance, not observed AWS capacity. One local 0.5-vCPU task sustained 100 RPS briefly; use 50 RPS per task and a 25x traffic peak budget. RDS scaling remains unverified.
notes.accounting: Twelve months and 512 bytes are storage-budget sensitivity inputs, not a financial-record retention policy. Raw answers remain 90 days; final merchant retention is unresolved.
notes.payment: US domestic-card reference 2.9% + USD 0.30 from Stripe pricing. Actual merchant country/currency/payment-method fees must replace this before launch. USD 5 is the optimistic average settlement at the current USD 5 threshold; month-end charges can be much smaller.
notes.identity: USD 100 is a provisional managed identity budget, not a Clerk quote or verified plan entitlement. Respondents are anonymous to the identity provider.
notes.labor: Forty SDK-maintenance hours and eight operations hours per month, plus 1.2 support minutes per active workspace, are explicit planning estimates, not measured payroll or support demand.
notes.network: Two zonal NAT gateways and four public IPv4 addresses budget one NAT and one minimum ALB address per AZ. Export traffic uses a future S3 gateway endpoint; NAT budget is control-plane traffic only.
notes.waf: AWS WAF published basic ACL/rule/request rates. No managed bot-control, CAPTCHA, marketplace or premium rules included; WAF is budgeted, not deployed.
notes.allowances: USD 25 covers an explicit placeholder for DNS, ECR, KMS, alarms and miscellaneous AWS operations. A 25% RDS-compute contingency is a budget, not a validated substitute for sizing or CPU-credit measurement.
notes.exclusions: No tax, negotiated discounts, free-tier allowances, premium AWS support, sales/customer acquisition, legal/compliance, general payroll or profit tax. Price-list first paid tiers are conservatively applied to all bytes. Costs are estimates, not bills.
